entity.name: Nullish Coalescing
entity.description: Return first value, or second value if first value is `null` or `undefined`.
entity.descriptionHtml: Return first value, or second value if first value is null or undefined.
entity.descriptionClean: Return first value, or second value if first value is null or undefined.

example.codeHighlighted: const foo = null ?? 'default string'; console.log(foo); // expected output: "default string" const baz = 0 ?? 42; console.log(baz); // expected output: 0

webFeature.description_html: The nullish coalescing (??) and nullish coalescing assignment (??=) operators return (or assign) its right-hand side operand when its left-hand side operand is null or undefined, and otherwise returns its left-hand side operand.
webFeature.name: Nullish coalescing

entity.name: Logical Assignment
entity.description: Operators to assign a value to a variable based on its own truthy/falsy status.
entity.descriptionHtml: Operators to assign a value to a variable based on its own truthy/falsy status.
entity.descriptionClean: Operators to assign a value to a variable based on its own truthy/falsy status.

example.codeHighlighted: const a = { duration: 50, title: '' }; a.duration ||= 10; console.log(a.duration); // expected output: 50 a.title ||= 'title is empty.'; console.log(a.title); // expected output: "title is empty"

webFeature.description_html: The logical AND assignment (&&=) and the logical OR assignment (||=) operators short-circuit the respective binary logical operators.
webFeature.name: Logical assignments

entity.descriptionClean: Provide the path to a specific JavaScript interpreter that you want to use to execute the script.

example.codeHighlighted: #!/usr/bin/env node console.log("Hello world");

webFeature.description_html: The #! comment at the absolute start of a script or module is treated as a normal comment and is ignored by the JavaScript engine.

entity.name: Iterator Methods
entity.description: Helper methods such as `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, and others applied to Iterators.
entity.descriptionHtml: Helper methods such as map, filter, reduce, and others applied to Iterators.
entity.descriptionClean: Helper methods such as map, filter, reduce, and others applied to Iterators.

example.codeHighlighted: function* factorials (n) { let result = 1; for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) { result *= i; yield result; } } const filteredFactorials = factorials(128).filter(x => x % 8 === 0);

resources.title: Iterator helpers have become Baseline Newly available

webFeature.description_html: The Iterator object is an abstract base for objects that implement the iterator protocol. It provides methods common to built-in iterators, such as filter(), find(), map(), and reduce(). You can also use the static method Iterator.from() to convert an existing iterable into an Iterator.
webFeature.name: Iterator methods

entity.name: `RegExp.escape`
entity.description: Escaping a string for use inside a Regular Expression.
entity.descriptionHtml: Escaping a string for use inside a Regular Expression.
entity.descriptionClean: Escaping a string for use inside a Regular Expression.

webFeature.description_html: The RegExp.escape() static method takes a string and replaces any characters that are potentially special characters of a regular expression with equivalent escape sequences. For example, RegExp.escape("[abc]") returns "\\[abc\\]".
webFeature.name: RegExp.escape()
